authorization: User: 开冲SOTA, following SCET-R design and explicit request for high-headroom entry points
scope: Real Falcon finite-controller recoverability diagnosis; no learned SCET-R model or SOTA claim
selection: From existing nonrandom174 development subset: collision failures with40..300 actions, one per scene; scenes ranked by eligible count then name; episode chosen by smallest SHA256(scene|episode); first4 scenes. No selection from intervention outcomes.
dataset_role: Failure-selected development only. Neither population success rate nor held-out evaluation. All selected episodes excluded from future confirmation.
baseline: Original frozen checkpoint with stochastic actions; new single-env runs are not expected to replicate old4-env trajectories
matching: Fresh seeded process replay from episode start. Baseline duplicated to full terminal. Branch prefixes must match all observations, recurrent inputs, sampled actions, other-agent actions, RNG and features before intervention. No unverified simulator snapshot restore.
schedule: One fresh reference and repeat per selected episode. If reference has no human collision, no interventions for that episode. Otherwise start at max(0,first_collision_zero_based_step-lead_steps). Deduplicate identical start/sequence. Resume original Falcon after sequence.
metrics: Terminal success,human_collision,SPL,PSC,steps,distance; repaired requires success==1 and human_collision==0. Delayed collision or timeout is not repaired.
failure_handling: Any prefix/replay/weight/termination mismatch fails validation; no candidate comparison reported as causal. Preserve failure outputs. No retries within allocation.
limitations: Oracle intervention timing uses reference collision and retrospective best candidate. This establishes only witnessed finite-library recoverability, not a deployable selector, general optimality gap, active-perception effect or population gain.
